title: BPP episode_request result (DESIGN.md §11.2, §14.8; registry R29 participant)
description: Success.result for episode_request (§11.2 record projection; gap notes G4, G27, G48): the Episode in prepared, or eligible when deterministic eligibility already holds; no lease yet (§14.8). It also PUBLISHES the stage-3 ResourceAllocation this call created and its portable_public binding digest — the exact value `placement_admit` compares — so stage 4 needs no out-of-band read (seam finding S-1), plus the frozen portable_public `parent_budget` fragment the subordinate side consumes and verifies (R3-L02, disposition D-R3-3): exact set/bridge refs and revisions, the set's cross-boundary digest, the kernel-derived stable key, and the exact parent items. A counterparty needs no naming convention and no caller-supplied parent fact.

resource_allocation_digest.description: The allocation's cross-boundary binding digest: SHA-256 over the `$domain`-tagged canonical `bpp-resource-allocation-binding-v0` fragment. `placement_admit` requires exactly these bytes.

parentBudgetFragment.description: The FROZEN portable_public parent-budget fragment (R3-L02, D-R3-3). Every member is byom's own committed fact about the §11.4 parent, and `digest` is SHA-256 over the `$domain`-tagged canonical bytes of exactly the other seven members — so the subordinate side verifies the fragment it was handed instead of naming references by convention (`rset-…`, `bridge-…`, `sub-…`) and taking the parent amount and account from its own caller's arguments.

byom_budget_reservation_set_digest.description: SHA-256 over the `$domain`-tagged canonical `bpp-budget-reservation-set-binding-v0` fragment `{reservation_set_id, revision, items}`. The row's own digest is byom's KEYED record commitment and is never a value a counterparty is asked to re-derive (amendment A8).

stable_external_reservation_key.description: Kernel-derived and persisted with the bridge BEFORE queueing (§11.4): published here, so the counterparty echoes it instead of deriving it from a name.

items.description: The EXACT parent §11.4 reservation items. A subordinate item pins one of these on all five coordinates and may narrow, never exceed (family contract L32).

digest.description: SHA-256 over the `$domain`-tagged canonical `bpp-parent-budget-fragment-v0` bytes of the seven members above.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset, semantically valid in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the pattern pins the lexical ranges and implementations MUST additionally reject impossible calendar instants (e.g. 2026-02-30) — the conformance runner enforces this on every vector; leap seconds are not accepted. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3, amended per RT-17).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.

portablePublicDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.2, D-R0-1; RT-02): this field commits to a PORTABLE structure a peer re-derives without a byom secret, so exactly class portable_public (unkeyed SHA-256) is acceptable. A well-constructed digest of any other class here is digest_class_mismatch — never a silent substitution.
